approach: Repair the documented Java/native-library startup failure with a bounded single-image Audiveris preflight before rerunning the existing integration pipeline.
objective: Inspect inherited recognition-command diagnostics and capture the exact startup exception. Correct only the implicated Java runtime or native-library dependency; retain the existing chord OCR thresholds and melody conversion. Spend at most 180 seconds establishing a real MusicXML export from one pilot image. If that succeeds, process all seven pilot images and independently parse each complete generated kern file, repairing serialization only where an actual parser diagnostic identifies a defect. If preflight fails, stop and retain the exact commands, runtime versions and exception rather than generating placeholder transcriptions. Never consult references or invent missing notes. Preserve raw recognition and chord bounding boxes; keep chord timing explicitly unaudited.
success_criteria: Deliver reproducible startup diagnostics and a real single-image MusicXML export as the first milestone. Then target seven independently parseable sealed predictions. Protected evaluation must compare melody error with the enlarged Audiveris baseline of 87/130 and both evaluated parents' 1.0 error; compare chord error with the earlier OCR parent's 25/38, the immediate parent's 38/38 and baseline's 30/38. Check upward-major-second transposition on actual generated notes, chord roots and slash basses, reporting untested cases separately. Successful startup or parsing alone must not be called musical correctness.
